text:
samir: quick post-sim summary — during the inter-region blackout test the ap-southeast primary kept accepting writes for tenant:acme even after it lost connectivity to control plane. forwarder couldn't talk to remote primary; writes accumulated ~15s of KV drift. seems our current policy favors availability too strongly in partition scenarios.

lucy: confirmed in logs. forwarder returned: "forwarder: remote-unreachable, residency=eu-only, action=drop" — but runtime still accepted the local write path because residency enforcement is async.

samir: that's the core gap: residency enforcement and forwarding decision race with local write acceptance. we need a deterministic per-tenant policy for short partitions.

ted: proposal: introduce a per-tenant write-gate with three states: open, restricted, locked.
- open = normal (accept writes, forward as configured)
- restricted = accept only idempotent/compensatable ops; return 409 for sensitive writes.
- locked = reject all non-read writes (409).

anya: legal check: restricted should still redact PII if writes are kept temporarily. we need a compliance flow to ensure no full-PII payloads are queued.

lucy: pragmatic implementation: when control-plane probe fails for >500ms, transition tenant -> restricted if residency prohibits cross-region writes. add short-circuit in the API layer so acceptance is deterministic (check header or local tenant-state).

samir: sample response header we can use so clients can react:
```http
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
X-Redwood-Write-Mode: restricted
Retry-After: 30
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "tenant_write_restricted",
  "details": "writes for this tenant are restricted due to region connectivity"
}
```

ted: metrics/obs plan: emit write_gate_state{tenant,region} gauge + write_rejected_total counter with reason tag. quick prom query to watch: `sum(rate(write_rejected_total[5m])) by (region)`

lucy: also add an audit event persisted to control-plane when a tenant transitions states so SRE/Legal can replay what happened. event must exclude payload.

samir: canary + rollout: feature-flag the write-gate with default off. enable for 5 low-volume tenants in staging, run chaos disconnects for 24h. regression criteria: total client-visible 5xxs don't increase >1.2x and reconcilers keep drift under 50ms tail.

ted: question: are we ok wrapping this into runtime 2.x? it touches core acceptance path. maybe implement as a middleware so minimal runtime change.

lucy: middleware + control-plane cache of tenant state. runtime can check cache locally with TTL. change should be small.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: write-gate-v1 -> staging clusters (deploy-bot)

anya: i'll queue legal signoff request; blocking item: what exact fields we persist in audit event (no payload allowed).

samir: decision: go ahead with write-gate middleware approach, telemetry + header, audit events (no payload), canary as described. i'll write the RFC and link here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/write-gate-1735551235 — PRs expected this week.

lucy: i'll follow-up with a tiny runbook for SRE: how to force tenant->open if control-plane recovers but we need manual override.

samir: thanks — syncing w/ infra to add the tenant-state cache TTL and a safe rollback path. short thread — more details in RFC.
